To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel brain targeting ligand RVG29 was exploited for efficient brain gene delivery and its cellular uptake was found to be mediated by clathrin and Caveolae dependent endocytosis.

PAMAM- PEG-RVG29/DNANPs are taken up by brain capillary cells via a clathrin- and caveolae-mediated endocytic process, that PAMAM-P EG-RVG29/D NA NPs are able to efficiently cross the BBB in vitro and in vivo, and that the PAMAM-PEG-RVG29/DA NAs show a higher brain gene expression than unmodified NPS.

the RVG29 peptide modified polyamidoamine (PAMAM)-PEG nanoparticles (NPs) were observed to be efficiently uptaken by brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs) through a caveolae and clathrin mediated endocytosis and were able to cross the blood-brain barrier in vitro and in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel gene delivery system for the brain.
the development of a novel noninvasive gene delivery strategy for brain diseases.
the brain-targeting gene therapy and provides a novel strategy for the treatment of brain diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RVG29 modified PAMAM/DNAs NPs can be used as a brain-targeting and gene delivery carrier.
the RVG peptide is a ligand for specific uptake by brain endothelial cells, and that the PAMAM-RVG29/DNAs NPs are an efficient gene delivery system for the central nervous system.
the PAMAM-RVG29/DNAs are internalized into the BCEC by a clathrin- and caveolae-mediated endocytosis, and the cellular uptake is related to GABA(B) receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RVG29 is a ligand for specific cellular uptake of NPs through clathrin and/or caveolae-mediated endocytosis, and the cellular uptake is related to the GABA receptor, not to the nAch receptor.
we successfully constructed a novel brain-targeting gene carrier based on RVG29 peptide and polyamidoamine (PAMAM), and investigated the cellular uptake mechanism of the carrier.
PAMAM-PEGRVG29 is an excellent ligand for brain-targeting gene therapy.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the modified rabies virus RVG29 is a promising ligand for brain-targeted gene delivery, and the specific cellular uptake mechanism is related with the GABA(B), but not the nicotinic acetycholine receptors.

the PEG-RVG29 conjugate could be used as a brain-targeting ligand to enhance the gene delivery efficiency across the blood-brain barrier, and the cellular uptake mechanisms of the NPs were also discussed.
RVG29 can be modified on PAMAM through PEG and the resulting NPs are capable of crossing the BBB and targeting brain cells.
